import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors1 = sns.color_palette('viridis', n_colors=10)
bars1 = ax1.barh(range(len(top_breeds)), top_breeds.values, color=colors1)
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(top_breeds)))
ax1.set_yticklabels(top_breeds.index)
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Registrations')
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds', fontweight='bold')
ax1.invert_yaxis()
for i, v in enumerate(top_breeds.values):
    ax1.text(v + 50, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 2: Dog Distribution by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
district_counts = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors2 = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', n_colors=len(district_counts))
bars2 = ax2.barh(district_counts.index, district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs')
ax2.set_title('Dog Distribution by District', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(district_counts.values):
    ax2.text(v + 20, i, str(int(v)), va='center', fontsize=8)

# Plot 3: Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
# Filter out invalid ages and get unique dog registrations
age_data = df[df['AlterVHundNum'].notna() & (df['AlterVHundNum'] >= 0) & (df['AlterVHundNum'] <= 20)]
age_counts = age_data['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts()
# Sort by numeric age
age_order = sorted(age_counts.index, key=lambda x: int(x.split('-')[0]) if x[0].isdigit() else 99)
age_counts_sorted = age_counts.reindex(age_order)
colors3 = sns.color_palette('Blues_d', n_colors=len(age_counts_sorted))
ax3.bar(range(len(age_counts_sorted)), age_counts_sorted.values, color=colors3)
ax3.set_xticks(range(len(age_counts_sorted)))
ax3.set_xticklabels(age_counts_sorted.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=8)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax3.set_title('Dog Age Distribution', fontweight='bold')

# Plot 4: Owner Age vs Dog Gender Distribution
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
# Create a crosstab of owner age and dog gender
owner_dog_data = df[df['SexHundLang'].notna() & (df['SexHundLang'] != 'Unbekannt')]
crosstab = pd.crosstab(owner_dog_data['AlterV10Lang'], owner_dog_data['SexHundLang'])
# Sort by age
age_sort_map = owner_dog_data.drop_duplicates('AlterV10Lang').set_index('AlterV10Lang')['AlterV10Sort']
crosstab = crosstab.reindex(sorted(crosstab.index, key=lambda x: age_sort_map.get(x, 99)))

x = range(len(crosstab))
width = 0.35
if 'männlich' in crosstab.columns:
    bars_male = ax4.bar([i - width/2 for i in x], crosstab['männlich'], width, label='Male Dogs', color='steelblue')
if 'weiblich' in crosstab.columns:
    bars_female = ax4.bar([i + width/2 for i in x], crosstab['weiblich'], width, label='Female Dogs', color='coral')

ax4.set_xticks(x)
ax4.set_xticklabels(crosstab.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=8)
ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Age Group')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax4.set_title('Dog Gender by Owner Age Group', fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend()

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
